text: New-user orientation
textPreview: New-user orientation

text:
Welcome participants. This session is designed for people new to the portal. By the end, they should be able to select a starting point, understand what happens after creation, and know where Codex fits.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide and Quick Start (reviewed 2026-08-03).
[/Sources]

Emphasize that the portal is not a generic app generator. It gives users a dependable, Cedarville-managed starting point so they can focus on the department need.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide and Quick Start (reviewed 2026-08-03).
[/Sources]

textPreview: Codex

text:
Clarify
Build
Explain
Improve
textPreview: Clarify | Build | Explain | Improve

text: Describe the app’s goal, users, and rules in plain language.
textPreview: Describe the app’s goal, users, and rules in plain language.

text: Ask Codex to make and explain changes in the managed repository.
textPreview: Ask Codex to make and explain changes in the managed repository.

text: Review the result, test the important task, then publish the version you trust.
textPreview: Review the result, test the important task, then publish the version you trust.

text:
Introduce Codex plainly: it is a collaborative coding agent. New users do not need to be programmers, but should be ready to explain their process, review outputs, and test the app’s key task. Avoid presenting Codex as an automatic approval or publishing authority.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide. Product framing for Codex is presenter guidance.
[/Sources]

text:
Encourage users to describe the business problem first. A form and approval path, a team tracker, or an information page are usually easier starting points than picking a runtime. When in doubt, choose the template whose examples are closest to the project.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide and Quick Start (reviewed 2026-08-03).
[/Sources]

textPreview: People need to search, filter, or update shared information.

textPreview: Use Cedarville login when…

textPreview: Only authorized Cedarville users should enter.

text: Choose these features because the app needs them—not because they sound useful.
textPreview: Choose these features because the app needs them—not because they sound useful.

text:
These are meaningful choices. A database and login can add capability, but they also add infrastructure and configuration. Tie the decision to the app’s actual behavior and audience.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide and Quick Start (reviewed 2026-08-03).

text: When to choose Create Only or Create & Publish
textPreview: When to choose Create Only or Create & Publish

text: Create Only
textPreview: Create Only

text: Choose this when the starter needs more customization or review before it is ready to deploy.
textPreview: Choose this when the starter needs more customization or review before it is ready to deploy.

text: Create & Publish
textPreview: Create & Publish

text: Choose this when the starter is ready for an initial Azure deployment and you want the portal to prepare the publishing path.
textPreview: Choose this when the starter is ready for an initial Azure deployment and you want the portal to prepare the publishing path.

text: In either case, keep the managed GitHub repository as the source of truth.
textPreview: In either case, keep the managed GitHub repository as the source of truth.

text:
Explain this in terms of readiness, not capability. Create Only is useful when a team needs time to work with Codex or a developer before a first deployment. Create & Publish follows the initial Azure path when the starter is appropriate for it.

[Sources]
Internal source: Cedarville App Portal User Guide and Quick Start (reviewed 2026-08-03).
